newsitem.title: INDIA: Police say 17 dead in India warehouse blast.
newsitem.headline: Police say 17 dead in India warehouse blast.

text.p: At least 17 people died on Thursday in two blasts at an explosives warehouse in the western state of Maharashtra on Monday, police said.

"We have recovered 17 bodies," Deputy Superintendent of Police Vijay Chavan told Reuters by telephone from the town of Satara in western Maharashtra. He said earlier reports by local news agencies that 38 people had died were incorrect.
Chavan said 31 people were injured in the two blasts, which occurred when gelatine was being unloaded from two vehicles for storage at the warehouse.
He said most of the casualties were among people living in the neighbourhood and between 30 and 40 houses in the Satara suburb of Sangam Nagar had been damaged by the blasts.
Asked if he thought the explosions were caused by sabotage, Chavan said: "Absolutely not." He described the gelatine as "minor explosives" used in mining and construction.
The injured had been taken to the Satara Civil Hospital, Chavan said, adding that police were waiting for debris to be cleared. Explosives experts were on the way to the site, he added.
